title: infectiousR: Access Infectious and Epidemiological Data via disease.sh API
text: infectiousR package provides seamless interface access real-time data infectious diseases disease.sh API, RESTful API offering global health statistics. package enables users explore --date information disease outbreaks, vaccination progress, surveillance metrics across countries, continents, U.S. states. includes set API-related functions retrieve real-time statistics COVID-19, influenza-like illnesses Centers Disease Control Prevention (CDC), vaccination coverage worldwide. Additionally, infectiousR offers built-function view datasets available within package. package also includes curated datasets infectious diseases influenza, measles, dengue, Ebola, tuberculosis, meningitis, AIDS, others — making comprehensive resource real-time monitoring historical analysis global infectious disease data.

title: infectiousR: Access Infectious and Epidemiological Data via disease.sh API
text: infectiousR package provides several core functions retrieve real-time infectious disease data disease.sh API. list main API-access functions included package: get_global_covid_stats() – Retrieves global COVID-19 statistics, including total cases, deaths, recoveries, . get_covid_stats_by_country_name() – Fetches COVID-19 statistics specific country name (e.g., “Brazil”, “India”). get_covid_stats_by_country() – Retrieves COVID-19 data countries. get_covid_stats_by_continent() – Retrieves COVID-19 data grouped continent. get_us_states_covid_stats() – Returns COVID-19 statistics U.S. states. get_covid_stats_for_state() – Retrieves data specified U.S. states (e.g., “NEW YORK”, “california”). get_influenza_cdc_ili() – Accesses influenza-like illness (ILI) data CDC. view_datasets_infectiousR() – Lists curated datasets available infectiousR package. functions enable users access --date, structured information infectious diseases, can combined tools dplyr ggplot2 powerful epidemiological analysis visualization. next section, ’ll explore use case demonstrate visualize COVID-19 data infectiousR.

what: US COVID-19 Statistics: Top 5 States by Total Cases
title: infectiousR: Access Infectious and Epidemiological Data via disease.sh API
code: # Load the COVID-19 data (from your package) covid_data <- get_us_states_covid_stats()  # Select the first 5 rows and remove columns with only NA values covid_clean <- covid_data %>%   slice_head(n = 5) %>%   select(where(~ !all(is.na(.))))  # Plot: Bar plot with different colors and readable y-axis (no scientific notation) ggplot(covid_clean, aes(x = reorder(state, -cases), y = cases, fill = state)) +   geom_bar(stat = "identity") +   scale_y_continuous(labels = function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE)) +   labs(     title = "COVID-19: Total Reported Cases by State (Top 5)",     x = "State",     y = "Total Cases"   ) +   theme_minimal() +   theme(legend.position = "none")

what: COVID-19 Case Rates in Latin America
title: infectiousR: Access Infectious and Epidemiological Data via disease.sh API
code: get_covid_stats_by_country() %>%   filter(country %in% c("Argentina", "Bolivia", "Brazil", "Chile", "Colombia",                        "Costa Rica", "Cuba", "Dominican Republic", "Ecuador",                        "El Salvador", "Guatemala", "Honduras", "Mexico")) %>%   select(-updated, -starts_with("today")) %>%   mutate(case_rate = (cases/population)*100000) %>%   ggplot(aes(x = reorder(country, -case_rate),           y = case_rate,           fill = country)) +   geom_col() +   scale_fill_manual(values = rainbow(n = 13)) +  # Built-in rainbow palette   labs(title = "COVID-19 Case Rates in Latin America",        subtitle = "Cases per 100,000 population",        x = NULL,        y = "Cases per 100k") +   theme_minimal() +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),         plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),         legend.position = "none")
